title: Adolescent Mental Health Outcomes Following Early Regulatory Problems
author: Matic Kadiš

steps.title: Configure environment and convert syntax
steps.instruction: Convert all provided .txt syntax files to .sps files and edit each file so that the working directory and all file paths point to your local analysis folder.

steps.title: Prepare raw cohort datasets
steps.instruction: Place the raw ALSPAC and Generation R datasets in the analysis folder, verify that their filenames match the load commands in the 1_RP_GenR and 1_ALSPAC_RP_syntax files, and ensure the participant‑ID variable names are consistent with those used in the syntax.

steps.title: Recode and rename variables
steps.instruction: Extract, rename, and recode the specified covariate and outcome variables as described in the study protocol.

steps.title: Process regulatory‑problem items
steps.instruction: Run the 1_RP_GenR and 1_ALSPAC_RP_syntax syntaxes on the raw cohort data to process parent‑reported crying, sleeping, and feeding items across infancy and toddlerhood, creating the exposure variables and saving the results as 1_RP_GenR.sav and 1_ALSPAC_RPs.sav.

steps.title: Harmonize cohort data
steps.instruction: Run the 2_GenR_data_harmonization and 2_ALSPAC_data_harmonization syntaxes on their respective datasets to produce harmonized files (2_GenR_Harmonized.sav, 2_ALSPAC_Harmonized.sav) containing covariates (sex, birth weight, gestational age, socioeconomic status, ethnicity, maternal prenatal depression, maternal prenatal anxiety, age at assessment) and mental‑health outcomes (Generation R: CBCL at ages 10, 14, 18; ALSPAC: SDQ at ages 9, 13, 17).

steps.title: Merge harmonized datasets
steps.instruction: Run the 3_merge syntax to pool 2_GenR_Harmonized.sav and 2_ALSPAC_Harmonized.sav into a single wide‑format dataset (3_Pooled_Wide.sav), generating a new sequential participant‑ID variable and a cohort indicator (Generation R = 1; ALSPAC = 2).

steps.title: Restructure to long format
steps.instruction: Run the 4_restructure syntax on 3_Pooled_Wide.sav to recode the data from wide to long format, saving the result as 4_Pooled_Long.sav.

steps.title: Run primary mixed‑model analyses
steps.instruction: Run the 5_main_analyses syntax on 4_Pooled_Long.sav to execute three sets of mixed models for each of the four harmonized mental‑health domains. Manually calculate effect sizes (Cohen’s d and pseudo partial η²) from the model outputs using the provided formulas.

steps.title: Impute missing covariate data
steps.instruction: Run the 6_imputation syntax on 4_Pooled_Long.sav. Use Fully Conditional Specification with a linear scale model (no interactions), generating 20 distinct imputations, each with a maximum of 10 iterations, for variables: sex, birth weight, gestational age, socioeconomic status, ethnicity, cohort, maternal depression and anxiety (raw and Z‑standardized), and age at assessment. Save the imputed dataset as 5_Pooled_Long_Imputed.sav.

steps.title: Re‑estimate models on imputed data
steps.instruction: Run the 7_mixed_model_imputed syntax on 5_Pooled_Long_Imputed.sav to re‑estimate the primary adjusted mixed models across the 20 imputed datasets.

steps.title: Dichotomize items and create indices
steps.instruction: Dichotomize raw continuous and categorical regulatory‑problem items, then sum them to create modality‑specific index scores (crying, sleeping, feeding) at each developmental timepoint.

steps.title: Classify RP domains
steps.instruction: Re‑dichotomize the modality indices to indicate presence or absence of each regulatory‑problem domain at each age.

steps.title: Assign trajectory groups
steps.instruction: Categorize participants into four mutually exclusive groups: (1) Never RP (zero or isolated RP), (2) Multiple RPs (≥2 domains concurrent at one timepoint), (3) Persistent RPs (any domain across ≥3 timepoints), (4) Multiple‑Persistent RPs (meets both multiple and persistent criteria).

steps.title: Z‑standardize maternal psychopathology
steps.instruction: Z‑standardize maternal prenatal depression and anxiety scores (both raw and Z‑standardized versions) to align scales across cohorts.

steps.title: Compute harmonized mental‑health domains
steps.instruction: Calculate the four harmonized mental‑health domains—emotional problems, peer‑relationship problems, hyperactivity/inattention, conduct problems—for each assessment age.

steps.title: Execute adjusted mixed models on imputations
steps.instruction: Run the main adjusted mixed models across the 20 imputed datasets for each mental‑health domain, testing early regulatory problems, assessment wave, and their interaction while adjusting for all covariates. Use REML estimation, a participant‑ID random intercept, and an AR(1) covariance structure for repeated measures.

steps.title: Pool p‑values across imputations
steps.instruction: Extract the 20 individual p‑values generated for each target effect across the imputation iterations and compute the median of these values to obtain the final pooled p‑value (required because SPSS does not automatically pool F‑values or pairwise comparisons for mixed models with imputed data).
